---
title: Rust quick start
description: Build an ACT component in Rust with the act-sdk macros.
---

## Scaffold

```bash
act-build init rust my-component
cd my-component
just init
```

`act-build init` carries the templates inside the binary — there is no `copier`, `uvx`, or Python
toolchain involved. Pass `--http` / `--fs` to have it declare those capabilities in `act.toml`
for you.

The template sets up `Cargo.toml` with a current [`act-sdk`](https://crates.io/crates/act-sdk), a `wit/` directory tracking [`act:tools`](https://github.com/actcore/act-spec/blob/main/wit/act-tools/act-tools.wit) (and [`act:sessions`](https://github.com/actcore/act-spec/blob/main/wit/act-sessions/act-sessions.wit) for stateful components) over [`act:core`](https://github.com/actcore/act-spec/blob/main/wit/act-core/act-core.wit), a `rust-toolchain.toml` pinning nightly + `wasm32-wasip2`, and a `justfile` with `build` / `test` / `publish` recipes.

## Write a tool

`src/lib.rs`:

```rust
use act_sdk::prelude::*;

#[act_component]
mod component {
    use super::*;

    #[act_tool(description = "Reverse a string", read_only)]
    fn reverse(
        /// Text to reverse
        text: String,
    ) -> ActResult<String> {
        Ok(text.chars().rev().collect())
    }
}
```

The `#[act_component]` macro generates the WIT `tool-provider` export. The `#[act_tool]` macro derives the JSON Schema from the function signature, collects `std:*` metadata (`read_only`, `idempotent`, `destructive`, `timeout_ms`), and registers the function with the component's dispatcher.

## Build

```bash
just build
```

This runs:
1. `cargo build --release` → `target/wasm32-wasip2/release/<name>.wasm`
2. `act-build pack <name>.wasm` → embeds the `act:component` custom section (CBOR-encoded metadata) and the contents of `skill/` as an Agent Skill tar.

## Verify

```bash
act info target/wasm32-wasip2/release/component_my_component.wasm --tools
```

Should print your component name, version, and the `reverse` tool with its auto-derived schema.

## Run

```bash
just test                    # e2e suite: pytest driving the component over MCP
act call <wasm> reverse --args '{"text":"hello"}'
```

## What `act-sdk` gives you

| Macro / type | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `#[act_component]` | Wraps a module as the `act:tools/tool-provider` export |
| `#[act_tool(…)]` | Registers a fn as a tool, emits JSON Schema from the signature + doc comments |
| `ActError` / `ActResult` | Return errors with a `std:*` kind and localized message |
| `Json<T>` | Opt into JSON encoding (default is CBOR, per [ACT-SPEC](https://github.com/actcore/act-spec/blob/main/spec/ACT-SPEC.md)) |
| `Content { mime, data }` | Return raw bytes with an explicit MIME type |
| `#[session_open]` / `#[session_close]` | Mark the session lifecycle hooks of a stateful component |
| `ActContext` / `SessionRegistry` | Per-call context and per-session state |

Agent Skills need no macro: `act-build pack` embeds a `skill/` directory automatically. See
[Agent Skills](/docs/build/skills/).
